title: Arithmetic and Probability Operations Generated by Bilateral Iteration of 2x −1
content: We construct arithmetic directly from positive and negative iterates of \(F(x) = 2^x - 1\).  At every fixed finite depth, inverse conjugation of the ordinary operations already gives exact associativity and distributivity.  Finite odds and log-odds coordinates keep the arithmetic inside the original coding interval.  We also retain the limiting constructions: the limits of \(G^n(F^n(x) + F^n(y))\) and \(G^{2n}(F^n(x)F^n(y))\), where \(G = F^{-1}\), make \([0,1)\) a commutative semiring with division by every nonzero element.  We prove uniqueness under local normalization and iteration compatibility, give an explicit derivative formula and an a priori evaluation certificate, and construct a real field on \((0,1)\) in which applying \(F\) is adding the field unit.  We reconnect these operations to the original marked greedy normalization code.  The opposite direction of iteration yields an increasing hierarchy of copulas in every dimension, with a uniquely normalized limit, a branching-process representation, and an explicit truncation bound permitting evaluation at arbitrarily large finite depths.  A power family has two exact resonances with diagonal probabilities equal to one or two forward iterates.  The unpowered limit has no lower diagonal tail-ratio limit, although the oscillation observed numerically is extremely small.  All statements concern the fixed map \(2^x - 1\).  The algebraic transport is classical; the results here concern the normalized rigidity, explicit limit bounds, and the probability identities for this fixed map.
